root_cause.text: In ntfs3's run_unpack(), the LCN range validation used unchecked 64-bit addition (`lcn + len`) when comparing against `sbi->used.bitmap.nbits`, allowing integer wraparound to bypass the volume boundary check for crafted large run values.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `if (lcn != SPARSE_LCN64 && lcn + len > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits)` with a `check_add_overflow(lcn, len, &lcn_end)` guard before comparing `lcn_end` to `sbi->used.bitmap.nbits`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that the raw addition could wrap around and bypass validation.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch replaces `if (lcn != SPARSE_LCN64 && lcn + len > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits)` with a `check_add_overflow(lcn, len, &lcn_end)` guard before comparing `lcn_end` to `sbi->used.bitmap.nbits`, and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that the raw addition could wrap around and bypass validation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix LCN range validation by detecting overflow in `lcn + len` before checking whether the extent exceeds the volume bitmap.
intent_record.what: The direct bounds check `if (lcn != SPARSE_LCN64 && lcn + len > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits)` was replaced with a nested `if (lcn != SPARSE_LCN64)` block that introduces a local `u64 lcn_end`, computes `lcn_end` using `check_add_overflow(lcn, len, &lcn_end)`, returns `-EINVAL` on overflow, and then compares `lcn_end` against `sbi->used.bitmap.nbits` to return `-EINVAL` if the LCN range exceeds the volume.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents unsigned addition overflow when calculating the end of the LCN range. Instead of potentially wrapping `lcn + len` and letting an invalid out-of-range extent pass the bounds check, the function now explicitly detects overflow and rejects the input, while still rejecting non-overflowing ranges that extend beyond the bitmap size.

grouping_result.intent: Fix LCN range validation by detecting overflow in `lcn + len` before checking whether the extent exceeds the volume bitmap.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds overflow detection for the unchecked 64-bit addition `lcn + len` before validating against the volume bitmap boundary in `run_unpack()`.

candidates.rationale: This bounds check directly embodies the bug: it uses unchecked 64-bit addition in `lcn + len`, so crafted large values can overflow and wrap, causing the comparison against `sbi->used.bitmap.nbits` to be bypassed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This boundary check performs unchecked 64-bit addition in `lcn + len` before comparing against `sbi->used.bitmap.nbits`. If `lcn + len` overflows, it can wrap to a smaller value and incorrectly pass the validation, allowing an out-of-range LCN extent to bypass the volume boundary check.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of `run_unpack()`, so it is sufficient to assess the vulnerable boundary check. The vulnerable construct is present in the validation `if (lcn != SPARSE_LCN64 && lcn + len > sbi->used.bitmap.nbits) { /* lcn range is out of volume */ return -EINVAL; }`. According to the root cause, the bug is the unchecked 64-bit addition `lcn + len` when validating against `sbi->used.bitmap.nbits`. In this commit, that exact unchecked addition is used directly. If `lcn + len` wraps around, the comparison can be bypassed. There is no overflow-safe check such as rearranging the comparison, checking `lcn > nbits - len`, or using an overflow helper before comparing. Therefore the function contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
